**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Track which task is awaiting skip confirmation**

When a user clicks Skip once and then changes the current task within the 3-second window (for example by pressing Start on another list item or Complete on the current task), `isSkipConfirming` stays true globally. The next click on the new task's Skip button bypasses this guard and immediately skips that different task, so the confirmation granted for one task can be reused for another; store the confirming task id or clear this state whenever `currentTaskId` changes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

`isSkipConfirming` can remain true if the current task changes via other actions (e.g. clicking another task/start/complete) within the 3s window. In that case, the next Skip click will execute immediately (no second-click safeguard), undermining the soft-confirmation intent. Cancel any pending skip confirmation whenever `currentTaskId` changes by clearing the timeout and resetting `isSkipConfirming`.

When the skip button enters confirmation mode, the `aria-label` becomes the generic "Confirm skip task", which loses the context (which task will be skipped / what happens next). For screen reader users this is a regression from the previous contextual label; keep the task title (and optionally the next task) in the confirm label too.

This assertion hard-codes the skip button `aria-label` ternary. If the confirm label is made contextual again (includes task title/next task), update this regex to match the new confirm branch so the test remains aligned with the intended accessibility behavior.
